text.p: Australian Mark Phillippoussis, the man with the biggest serve in the game, upset 10th-seeded Andre Agassi 7-6 (7-5) 7-6 (7-5) in the first round of the Champions Cup on Tuesday.
The Agassi and Philippoussis battle was billed as a match between the the best server versus the best return of server.
Although the 13th-ranked Agassi came out on the losing side today, he was able to accomplish one thing.

He was able to break the 32nd-ranked Philippoussis' serve once in the 56-minute match. He failed to break his opponents' service in his last three matches. Javier Sanchez sent Agassi packing in the first round, Gustavo Kuerten dispatched him in the second round, and Greg Rusedski turned him back in the semifinals.
Philippoussis, who won last week's Scottsdale event, served a record breaking 142 mph (228.5 kph) ace at that Arizona based tournament.
"It's my biggest weapon, but I can hit winners with my forehand, backhand and come in and volley," Philippoussis said.
The Australian served 23 aces to Agassi's one in the match.
"It is a big serve," Agassi said. "I had my looks at break points. I certainly would be optimistic returning it again."
Agassi, a former top-ranked player, who has a 5-8 win- loss record since playing the 1996 U.S. Open in September, has only competed in four tournaments this year.
"It is definitely about the intensity inside each point and the desire to want to win every point," Agassi said. "You know, I'm not just out there for the hell of it. My desire is definitely there."
The first set was hard fought, with neither player facing a break point on serve. Serving at 6-5 in the first set tiebreaker, Philippoussis won the set when Agassi dumped a forehand into the net.
In the second set, both players broke serve once as they headed for the face-off in the tiebreaker.
At 5-5 in the second set tiebreaker, Phillippoussis ended the match with two winners -- a rocket ace followed by a screeching forehand crosscourt passing shot.
"On the big points in the tiebreakers, I played well," Philippoussis said. "I went for some big winners."
